what_it_requires: AI can’t provide therapy, make treatment decisions, talk with clients in a therapeutic way, or detect emotions. You may use it for scheduling, billing, notes and similar support. You need written consent before AI records or transcribes a session.
Providers can’t use AI to deliver mental or behavioral health care directly. Admin uses like scheduling, billing and notes are allowed. No one can market an AI as a therapist.
Same idea as Illinois. You also can’t refuse care to a client who says no to AI.
Same idea as Illinois, plus written consent before AI records a session. One consent can cover later sessions. You can’t refuse care to a client who says no.

penalty_or_enforcer: State health agency (EOHHS) and existing penalties

what_it_requires: Using AI in ways the law forbids counts as unprofessional conduct for mental health professionals.
No one can advertise an AI system as a qualified mental health professional.
Rules for mental health chatbots, not a ban. Sellers must say it’s AI, label ads, and can’t sell or share users’ health information.
